new_statements.quote: [§6] Le fang ntúmú est une langue tonale à deux ou trois registres (haut, moyen, bas), et accentuelle sur la première syllabe de la base (racine ou thème nominal). [...] [§24] Nous avons vu plus haut que le fang ntúmú est à la fois tonale et accentuel. Nous constatons que les locuteurs marquent toujours une légère pause après le préfixe nominal. [...] [§25] Nous constatons en outre que la première syllabe de la base (thème ou racine verbo-nominale) est toujours accentuée. En fait pause et accent sont étroitement liés. [...] [§26] En fang ntúmú, l'accent remplit donc une fonction démarcative en ce sens qu'il permet d'identifier non seulement la limite du préfixe nominal, mais également la première syllabe de la base.
new_statements.translation: [§6] Fang Ntumu is a tone language with two or three registers (high, mid, low), and accentual on the first syllable of the base (root or nominal stem). [§24] We saw above that Fang Ntumu is both tonal and accentual. We observe that speakers always mark a slight pause after the noun prefix. [§25] We further observe that the first syllable of the base (stem or verbo-nominal root) is always accented. In fact pause and accent are closely linked. [§26] In Fang Ntumu, accent thus fulfils a demarcative function in that it identifies not only the boundary of the noun prefix but also the first syllable of the base.
new_statements.citation: Ollomo Ella, Régis. 2012. Le pluriel en fang ntumu. Corela (Cognition, représentation, langage) HS-11 [en ligne, mis en ligne le 2 avril 2012]. Université de Poitiers. DOI: 10.4000/corela.2520.
new_statements.locator: para. 6 (PDF p. 2) and section 2.3 'Nouvelles considérations', paras. 24-26 (PDF p. 6)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: (9 pp., text layer, Corela HS-11, DOI 10.4000/corela.2520, CC BY-NC-SA per the PDF's own cover page). extracted text per page confirms the locators: para 6 is on PDF p.2 ('Le fang ntúmú est une langue tonale à deux ou trois registres (haut, moyen, bas), et accentuelle sur la première syllabe de la base (racine ou thème nominal).') and paras 24-26 (section 2.3 'Nouvelles considérations') are on PDF p.6; every sentence in the reported quote matches the PDF word for word, the [..] marks only skip one sentence of para 24 ('Ceci vaut aussi bien pour les nominaux posant un problème de découpage morphologique..') and the examples under para 25 (7) A'kɔ́ʔ 'pierre' |à-kɔ́ʔ|, Mə̀'kɔ́ʔ 'pi…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tone language (H/M/L) with a word accent fixed on the stem-initial (root-initial) syllable; noun-class prefixes are unaccented, so accent is demarcative of the prefix-stem boundary (e.g. à-'kɔ́ʔ 'stone', mə̀-'kɔ́ʔ 'stones').
new_statements.exceptions: None; stated as exceptionless ('toujours accentuée'). Idiatov & Van de Velde 2016 (instrumental slides) add that within A70 the relative lengthening of the stem-initial consonant 'appears to decline in the extreme south of the domain'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (nominal and verbo-nominal bases in citation forms); data Ntumu dialect recorded 1997 at Mvi-Mangale, south Cameroon (M.-F. Rombi). Statement is a background remark in a noun-morphology article, not a dedicated phonology; corroborated instrumentally (stem-initial C-lengthening in Fang) by Idiatov & Van de Velde 2016 slides, and the naive Spanish-style 'agudas/llanas/esdrújulas' examples in Ndongo Esono 1956 (me-kók, a-kála, me-kémele) are consistent with prefix + stem-initial stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Ntumu dialect of Fang (Glottolog dialect ntum1238 'Ntum', A75A; northern Gabon / southern Cameroon / Río Muni), data from Mvi-Mangale, south Cameroon. Idiatov & Van de Velde's instrumental data cover several regional Fang varieties (Okak shown). Other examined descriptions cover Medouneu, Cocobeach, Bitam (Medjo Mvé), Río Muni (Bibang Oyee, Ndongo Esono 'pamue') varieties of the same language fang1246.

sources.note: Lección II 'El acento' (pp. 14-15): 'Todas las palabras tienen acento.. Acento es la mayor fuerza de voz con que se pronuncia una sílaba de cada palabra'; classifies words Spanish-style as agudas (me-kók 'piedras', bi-lám, me-tók), llanas (a-kála 'esteras', e-sángo), esdrújulas (me-kémele 'savias') -- naive but the examples are consistent with prefix + stem-initial stress. sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Says nothing about stress placement, so it neither confirms nor contradicts Ollomo Ella's 'accent on the first syllable of the base'. It is also a different variety: the Fang of the Djoum region (village Esson, S. Cameroon, Guthrie A74 in the author's terms), with ntumu and mvae named as neighbouring parlers in the Ntem and Océan départements (pp. 9-10, 51 n.1).
